pumac-2022-number-theory-a-07.title: Multiplicativity and prime powers
pumac-2022-number-theory-a-07.body:
**Multiplicative.** If $\gcd(m,n)=1$, a residue mod $mn$ is a square iff its residues mod $m$ and mod $n$ are squares (Chinese Remainder Theorem), so $f(mn)=f(m)f(n)$. Since $225^k=3^{2k}5^{2k}$, it suffices to find $f(p^{2k})$ for an odd prime $p$.

**Squares mod $p^{2k}$ ($p$ odd).** Classify a residue $r$ by its $p$-adic valuation. A square has even valuation, so either $r=0$ or $r=p^{2j}u$ with $0\le j\le k-1$ and $u$ a unit modulo $p^{2k-2j}$. Such an $r$ is a square iff $u$ is a square modulo $p^{2k-2j}$, and (Hensel's lemma, $p$ odd) a unit is a square mod $p^t$ iff it is a square mod $p$. Hence exactly half of the $\varphi(p^t)=(p-1)p^{t-1}$ units are squares. With $i=k-j$ this gives
$$f(p^{2k})=1+\frac{p-1}2\sum_{i=1}^{k}p^{2i-1}.$$
Dividing by $p^{2k}$ and putting $j=k-i$,
$$\frac{f(p^{2k})}{p^{2k}}=p^{-2k}+\frac{p-1}{2p}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}p^{-2j}\ \longrightarrow\ \frac{p-1}{2p}\cdot\frac{p^2}{p^2-1}=\frac p{2(p+1)}\quad(k\to\infty).$$

For $p=3$ this is $\frac38$ and for $p=5$ it is $\frac5{12}$, so the limit is $\frac38\cdot\frac5{12}=\frac5{32}$, and $p+q=5+32=37$. (For example $f(225)/225=0.1956$ and $f(225^2)/225^2=0.1598$, approaching $0.15625$.)

**Answer: 37**

pumac-2022-number-theory-a-08.title: Swap the order of summation
pumac-2022-number-theory-a-08.body:
$\lfloor160/n\rfloor$ counts the multiples of $n$ that are at most $160$, so
$$\sum_{n=1}^{160}(-1)^{\omega(n)}\left\lfloor\frac{160}n\right\rfloor=\sum_{N=1}^{160}g(N),\qquad g(N)=\sum_{d\mid N}(-1)^{\omega(d)}.$$
The function $(-1)^{\omega(d)}$ is multiplicative, hence so is $g$, and for a prime power
$$g(p^e)=1+\underbrace{(-1)+\dots+(-1)}_{e}=1-e .$$
In particular $g(p)=0$, so $g(N)=0$ whenever some prime divides $N$ exactly once. Only $N\le160$ all of whose prime exponents are at least $2$ matter ("powerful numbers"): $1$; the prime powers $4,8,16,32,64,128$, $9,27,81$, $25,125$, $49$, $121$; and the products $36,72,144,108,100$.

Values of $g$: $g(1)=1$; $g(p^e)=1-e$: $4\to-1$, $8\to-2$, $16\to-3$, $32\to-4$, $64\to-5$, $128\to-6$, $9\to-1$, $27\to-2$, $81\to-3$, $25\to-1$, $125\to-2$, $49\to-1$, $121\to-1$; and $g(36)=g(4)g(9)=1$, $g(72)=g(8)g(9)=2$, $g(144)=g(16)g(9)=3$, $g(108)=g(4)g(27)=2$, $g(100)=g(4)g(25)=1$.

Sum: $1+(-21)+(-6)+(-3)+(-1)+(-1)+(1+2+3+2+1)=1-21-6-3-1-1+9=-22$. (Direct evaluation of the original sum also gives $-22$.)

The absolute value is $22$.

**Answer: 22**
